messages:
Alex K.: heads-up - intermittent OOMs on H100 when KV paging is enabled for very long contexts (>=120k tokens). crash occurs in page-table eviction path, looks like a null deref.
Priya S.: repro steps? any logs/backtrace?
Alex K.: minimal repro: run long_ctx_integration with model=redwood-7b, seq=131072, batch=1, KV_PAGING=1, KV_PAGE_SIZE=64KB. mem grows ~2GB/step until OOM. attaching backtrace snippet below:
```
#0 0x7fabc.. in paged_attn.cu:handle_eviction()
#1 0x7fabd.. in kv_cache_pop_page()
#2 0x7fabe.. in serve_step()
```
We see free-list pointer read becomes 0x0, then crash when dereferencing entry->next.
Rick O.: can you paste the nvprof / nsight summary? any unusual memcpy kernels?
Alex K.: nvprof shows a fallback memcpy kernel on H100 when pages are fragmented; bandwidth drops ~35%. pprof flame shows a tight hotspot in reclaim loop.
Emily Z.: saw related behavior on A100 under heavy concurrency. sounds like ABA on the free list + a race in page refcount decrement. we had a change months ago that reordered CAS/dec which might be related.
Priya S.: severity? needs P0?
Emily Z.: reproducible locally, but only under high contended evictions. I'd mark P1 but moving to P0 if production repro.
Alex K.: quick repro script: git rev 9f3b2c, env: KV_PAGE_SIZE=65536, KV_MAX_PAGES=4096, USE_CUDA_MEMPOOL=1. run: `./run_long_ctx --model redwood-7b --seq 131072 --kv-paging`
bench-bot: perf alert: paged-evict throughput regressed 18% on L4 after kernel-selection change (compare master->HEAD).
Rick O.: that matches a theory: when pages are non-contiguous we fall back to a generic memcpy kernel instead of the fast page-batched path. fragmentation affects kernel selection heuristics.
Priya S.: short-term mitigations? stricter allocation alignment or immediate compaction during low-load windows?
Alex K.: proposed patch: add a 64-bit generation counter to free-list entries to avoid ABA (`pack = (gen<<48) | idx`) + an assert on pointer parity. quick PoC reduces repro frequency in my H100 runs.
Emily Z.: also propose an idle-time compaction job that coalesces holes and updates page-table indexes. we should be careful with pin/unpin semantics while compacting.
Rick O.: another edge I noticed: when allocation fails we sometimes skip updating owner ptr on failure path - small leak + stale entry that later gets reclaimed -> corruption.
Priya S.: can both of you run the repro across H100, A100, and L4 and paste nvprof + serve logs? add everything to an issue.
Alex K.: I'll run H100 and L4 today and attach logs. initial H100 run: nvprof shows memcpy fallback when >40% pages fragmented, confirming the hypothesis.
Emily Z.: running A100 now, also seeing a failed CAS on free-list head in the trace (race). attaching short diff that reorders the CAS -> fixed immediate double-free in my local run.
Priya S.: created incident INF-8472 and added triage checklist. please add PRs to the issue.
deploy-bot: created issue INF-8472 and linked this thread.
Alex K.: note: flamegraphs show reclaim loop occupies ~22% CPU and kernel selection overhead ~12% when fragmentation present. fixing should recover ~15-20% throughput.
Emily Z.: found small leak in page_table->owner on error path; I'll open a small PR for that first.
Priya S.: good. assign eng-runtime and eng-infra to coordinate. update thread with PR links. thanks all :rocket:
